content: Gratitude is not only the greatest of virtues, but the parent of all the others.
author: Marcus Tullius Cicero
story:
Watching the Roman Republic collapse into military dictatorship and civil war, Cicero used his oratorical mastery to defend constitutional liberty, paying with his life when Mark Antony's soldiers assassinated him in 43 BC. In his final philosophical writings, he articulated the immortal duties of civic honor, moral justice, and courageous friendship.

In formulating this reflection, Marcus Tullius Cicero stripped away superficial conventions to address the core anatomy of gratitude. For Marcus Tullius Cicero, true wisdom is never an abstract luxury, but an urgent practical discipline required to navigate life with clarity and unshakeable dignity.
